doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Full Swing and the first lyric, Tommy Newsom's tune
summary: Feather's vocal group Full Swing, formed by Richard Perry and Joel Silver, leads to her first lyric, 'The Trocadero Ballroom', which Perry makes her rewrite.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So I was in this vocal group called Full Swing that was put together by Richard Perry, at that time a huge pop producer, and Joel Silver, a big movie producer. And they had this idea to have an updated big band with three vocalists in front of it. So they hired me and Charlotte Crossley, who was in “Jesus Christ Superstar” with me and also was a Harlette with Bette Midler, and Steve March Torme, Mel Torme’s son. So he was looking for songs for us to record. This is the first time I had an actual record deal so it was very exciting and Richard was living a glamorous life and he had Planet Records and Studio 55 — or was it Studio 54? No it was Studio 55. One of them was a nightclub. But so he wanted to go out to Donte’s the jazz club in L.A. that was very popular at the time, to © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

hear Tommy Newsom’s big band. We heard this song called “La Bem” that Tommy had written, and then we had a meeting with Richard and he said, “I want to have lyrics to that song. I think we should hire a lyricist.” And for some reason I said, “I could do it.” I hadn’t really written lyrics all that much. I had made some attempts at writing kind of quasi-pop songs when I was in my late 20s. I was 32 at the time of this meeting. But I had grown up listening to Lambert, Hendricks & Ross and trying to sing along with my mom. So I knew what it was to write complicated words to complicated pieces of music, and it just seemed like something that would be fun to try. So I said, “Well I can do it.” And I went oh, okay. I went home, I wrote lyrics to this Tommy Newsom piece and I brought them back and I sang it through for Richard and the other two, and they were kind of quiet. And he said, “Well I don’t like it at all. It should be completely different. It should be about —” this, this, this and that, and I was furiously scribbling away. So I went home and re-did it, brought it back, he said, “Yeah I like it. We’ll record that.” And I wound up writing lyrics for half the album but it just came so naturally to me, not that it was easy but it was so organic. It was easier than singing, it was easier than anything I’ve ever tried to do before — dancing which I attempted for many years, acting which I love but never made much of a splash at, and it just took over my life from that point onward, I loved it so much.
Can you tell me the name of the tune again, the Tommy Newsom tune?

The title was “The Trocadero Ballroom.” It was like the opera, La B-O-E — no actually it was something else it was a play on words that was not the same as the opera but it was something like La Boheme. And then my title was “The Trocadero Ballroom” ‘cause Richard said, “It should be about a ballroom and everybody wants to go there and it’s very glamorous, they’re doing cocaine — mind you, it was the 80s so that’s —
